report.releaseDate: 13 Nov 2026 (after market close; 10-Q filed same day)
report.currency: USD (reporting currency; tables in US$ thousands unless stated)
report.verdict: A pre-revenue pivot dressed up as a quarter: online-casino net gaming revenue fell 51% YoY (-15% QoQ) to $2.4m, adj. EBITDA sank to -$2.1m (-87% margin) and the ROLR prediction-markets platform contributed $0 while absorbing the marketing and capex. Net cash of $13.4m (no debt) against ~$4.7m of Q3 cash consumption (incl. capex) buys roughly three quarters at the current rate, and management will not disclose any launch KPIs until March 2027 — the stock (-15.5% on the first post-results session) priced that information vacuum.

kpis.label: Share price (16 Nov, first session post-results)

summary: **Headline miss on every P&L line, no consensus to hide behind.** Net revenue $2,395k (-51% YoY from $4,858k; -15% QoQ from $2,809k), loss from operations -$2,719k (vs -$703k), pre-tax loss -$2,596k (vs -$758k), GAAP net loss -$2,780k / -$0.25 per share versus +$3,667k / +$0.39 diluted a year ago — but the prior-year figure was flattered by a $3.6m deferred-tax valuation-allowance release at a Maltese subsidiary and $0.8m of discontinued-ops income. Only two small-cap brokers (Alliance Global Partners, Dawson James) were on the call; there is no meaningful published consensus.

**Adj. EBITDA -$2,094k (margin -87.4%) vs -$162k (-3.3%) in Q3-25 and -$1,823k (-65%) in Q2-26.** Add-backs are modest (SBC $421k, D&A $99k, FX loss $97k, tax $184k, net interest income -$115k), so the adjusted and GAAP pictures are close. 9M adj. EBITDA -$5,180k vs -$3,337k.

**The quarter is a pre-revenue pivot: ROLR prediction markets booked $0 in Q3 and 9M.** The platform ran an invitation-only beta from 15 Sep, launched publicly on 21 Oct, the iOS app went live on 9 Nov and Android is slated for Q4. Management framed Q3 as 'the last quarter in which prediction markets appear only on the expense side of the ledger' and 2027 as the first full year, with prediction markets expected to be 'the major growth driver'.

**Casino shrinkage is deliberate but severe.** Unique depositing customers fell ~77% to ~4,723 (from 20,128), active users ~75% to ~5,448 (from ~21,800), wagers ~64% to ~$53m (from >$146m) and first-time depositors ~95% [KPI levels per a secondary summary of the 10-Q MD&A; they reconcile exactly to the company's $507 ARPU and the CEO's '35% more on every dollar wagered']. ARPU per depositing customer doubled to $507 (+110%) and hold rose to ~4.5% from ~3.3%.

**Geographic concentration is rising, not falling.** Finland was $1,618k or 67% of net gaming revenue (-40% YoY; 56% share a year ago), New Zealand $522k / 22% (-57%), Canada $208k / 9% (-65%), Norway $0 (exited; $267k LY) and RoW $47k. The exits (Norway, Sweden non-core services, Casino Room domain) are done; what remains is a Finland/NZ book.

**New Zealand exit on 1 Dec removes ~22% of casino revenue.** The company has elected not to apply under NZ's new limited-licence regime; the CFO guided that casino revenue will 'step down further from December with a full effect from the first quarter of 2027'. Finland (67% of revenue) moves to a licensed regime from 2027 — the company has not disclosed its licensing intentions [unverified; background knowledge, not from the filings read].

**Opex fell 8% YoY to $5,114k but the mix tells the story.** Direct operating costs -59% to $808k (33.7% of revenue vs 40.8%), G&A +8% to $3,050k (127% of revenue), advertising & promotions +84% YoY and +94% QoQ to $1,009k (42% of revenue) as ROLR launch marketing started, and expensed product/software development +17% to $247k. Opex is now 2.1x revenue.

**Related-party marketing is now the majority of A&P.** $541k of Q3 advertising spend (54% of the total) went to the affiliated marketing partner Spike Up Media (vs $92k in Q3-25 and $280k in Q2-26), plus a $333k related-party prepaid on the balance sheet. A Dawson James analyst noted on the call that several named distribution partners are owned by shareholders; management declined to disclose the marketing allocation.

**Cash $13.4m (+$0.4m restricted), zero borrowings, equity $27.3m.** Cash fell $4.6m in the quarter. 9M operating cash outflow was -$8,879k (vs -$4,526k) and investing -$3,590k (vs -$480k), almost all capitalised ROLR platform development (~$1.7m in Q3 alone). 9M cash consumption of $12.5m ≈ $1.4m/month implies ~10 months of runway at that rate (≈8.5 months at the Q3 rate); management nonetheless asserts sufficiency for 'at least the next twelve months'.

**The balance sheet was rebuilt by equity, not operations.** January 2026 registered direct offering of 1,892,506 shares at $13.21 ($25.0m gross, ~$3.5m costs incl. $1.0m of placement-agent warrants) plus a $1.0m private placement at $2.80; net financing inflow $23.5m. Weighted diluted shares rose 30% YoY to 11.0m; 11,043,795 shares outstanding at 13 Nov. The stock at $2.56 sits ~81% below the RDO price; market cap ~$28m, of which net cash is ~47%.

**Restatement and control weaknesses.** On 16 Oct the company filed 10-Q/As for Q1 and Q2 2026 to reclassify the $1.0m placement-agent warrant cost from G&A to APIC, cutting the Q1 net loss to $2.0m from $3.0m and H1 to $4.3m from $5.3m (no effect on cash, equity or adj. EBITDA). Two material weaknesses in ICFR remained unremediated at 30 Sep [per secondary summary of 10-Q Item 4; not read directly].

**Regulatory structure: guaranteed introducing broker, with Crypto.com holding the keys.** ROLR US LLC is an NFA-registered guaranteed introducing broker (licence 24 Jun 2026); Crypto.com FCM carries customer accounts and CDNA is the exclusive contract provider for 24 months from April 2026. The filing gives no take-rate or revenue-share disclosure — the single most important unknown in the model.

**Strategic optionality being built, none of it monetised yet.** ROLR FCM LLC formed 11 Nov with Connamara engaged to explore an FCM application (which management says would sit outside the Crypto.com exclusivity); ProphetX agreement (12 Nov) only becomes effective six months after FCM registration; NFA commodity-trading-advisor registration obtained ahead of an undisclosed 'very powerful' product release before end-November; DCM/DCO licences floated as future options.

**Technology is now owned, not rented.** The 13 Aug source-code licence and development agreement with DeepEther Labs (mrkts.com) gives ROLR ownership of the customer-facing application; intangible assets rose to $13.9m from $10.5m at Dec-25. Senior hires: Flip Pidot (CBO, ex-prediction-markets veteran) and Ben Sutherland (SVP Product, ex-Greentube USA CEO).

**Management is withholding launch data.** Asked directly for CAC, sign-ups, volume or milestones, the CEO said it was 'too early' and that the company would consider what to release 'when the time is right' — i.e. the first look at unit economics comes with FY results in March 2027, covering roughly ten weeks of trading.

**Industry framing vs reality.** Management cites Bernstein's ~$410bn 2026 prediction-market volume estimate and $10tn by 2035; on the same day Meta reportedly entered the category, and the CEO acknowledged state-level litigation shapes a state-by-state marketing plan. ROLR is a sub-scale introducing broker entering against Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood, DraftKings and FanDuel/CME with ~$13m of cash.

**Share-price reaction: -7.1% to $3.03 on 13 Nov ahead of the after-close release, -7.3% after hours to $2.81, then -15.5% to $2.56 on 16 Nov, the first full session.** 52-week range $1.16–$33.68 — the January prediction-markets spike has fully unwound.

**Thesis read-through: the equity is an option on ROLR unit economics with a short fuse.** The casino is a melting ice cube (Finland concentration, NZ exit, ~15%/qtr sequential decline), G&A alone exceeds revenue, and the funding plan beyond mid-2027 almost certainly requires equity at depressed prices unless Q4/Q1 ROLR traction is material. Net cash per share ~$1.21 and book value ~$2.48/share are the only hard anchors.

segments.name: Online casino (High Roller / Fruta / Kassuuu — Estonia-licensed; Finland, New Zealand, Canada)
segments.headline: Revenue -51% YoY to $2.4m on a 77% smaller depositing base; ARPU doubled to $507 and contribution margin rose to 66%, but Finland is now 67% of a book that loses New Zealand (22%) on 1 Dec.
narrative: They reported net gaming revenue of $2,395k, down 50.8% from $4,865k a year earlier and 14.7% lower than Q2's $2,809k, which itself had fallen 16.5% sequentially from Q1's $3,366k — the sequential decay rate has been remarkably steady at roughly 15% a quarter since the strategic review. Management attributes the decline to the markets exited during 2025 (Norway, the Swedish non-core services line and the Casino Room domain, now in discontinued operations) and to a 'revised marketing strategy', which in practice means acquisition spend for casino has been cut to almost nothing. The business today is a retention exercise run through the Estonian licence held by Happy Hour Solutions, acquired on 31 December 2025 in exchange for the Casino Room domain.

The customer base has been allowed to shrink by roughly three-quarters: unique depositing customers were about 4,723 against 20,128 in Q3-25 (-77%), active users roughly 5,448 against ~21,800 (-75%), and first-time depositors fell ~95% — levels we take from a secondary summary of the 10-Q MD&A, but which reconcile precisely to the company-reported revenue and $507 ARPU. Wagers dropped ~64% to ~$53m from more than $146m, so revenue fell less than volume: hold rose to ~4.5% of wagers from ~3.3%, which is what the CEO meant by 'earning roughly 35% more on every dollar wagered'. Average revenue per depositing customer more than doubled to $507 from $242. That is a genuine mix improvement — fewer bonus-driven low-value accounts — but it is not evidence of pricing power; with a base this small, a handful of VIPs and ordinary casino variance can move the quarterly ARPU materially in either direction.

Geographically the book has collapsed into Finland. Finnish net gaming revenue was $1,618k, down 39.8% YoY, but its share rose to 67% from 56%; New Zealand was $522k (-57%, 22% share), Canada $208k (-65%, 9%), Norway nil against $267k, and the rest of the world $47k. For the nine months Finland contributed $5,543k (65%) and New Zealand ~22% (~$1.9m). On 1 December New Zealand moves to a limited-licence regime and the company has chosen not to apply, so that 22% disappears from December with full effect in Q1-27 — roughly $0.17m lost in Q4 and ~$0.5m a quarter thereafter at the current run-rate. Finland's own transition to a licensed market from 2027 is the next regulatory cliff; the filings we read do not say whether High Roller intends to seek a Finnish licence, and the Ontario launch flagged a year ago ('estimated H1 2026') has gone quiet. Canada at $208k is grey-market revenue under the Estonian licence.

Cost discipline is the better half of the story. Direct operating costs (payment providers, game suppliers, affiliate revenue share) fell 59% to $808k, or 33.7% of revenue from 40.8%, so revenue less direct costs of $1,587k was only 2% below Q2's $1,619k despite the 15% revenue drop, and the contribution margin reached 66.3% versus 59.2% a year ago and 57.6% in Q2. The company does not allocate G&A or marketing to the casino, so segment EBITDA cannot be derived; with group G&A of $3,050k against total revenue of $2,395k, the casino is in any case a cash contributor only at the contribution line. Advertising for the casino is now minimal — group A&P of $1,009k is overwhelmingly ROLR launch preparation.

Management's guidance for the segment is unambiguously downward: casino revenue will 'step down further from December' with the NZ exit fully visible in Q1-27, and the CEO told investors that using the casino top line as a barometer for the company means 'focusing on the wrong thing'. We model Q4 casino revenue of roughly $2.0–2.2m and a Q1-27 run-rate nearer $1.6–1.8m (estimates: ~10% underlying sequential attrition plus the NZ removal), with contribution margin holding in the mid-60s. The practical function of this segment is to fund a slice of corporate overhead while ROLR scales; it is not an asset a buyer would pay much for given the licence footprint and customer concentration.

segments.name: ROLR prediction markets (US) — guaranteed introducing broker via Crypto.com FCM / CDNA
segments.headline: Pre-revenue in Q3 ($0); public launch 21 Oct, iOS 9 Nov; marketing and capex ramping with no disclosed KPIs until March 2027; take-rate with CDNA undisclosed.
narrative: They generated no prediction-markets revenue in the three or nine months to 30 September: the invitation-only beta with real money and real markets began on 15 September, the public launch on desktop and mobile web followed on 21 October, the iOS app reached the App Store on 9 November and an Android release is targeted before year-end subject to Google approval. The CFO stated plainly that Q4 'will be the first to include prediction markets revenue', covering roughly ten weeks of trading, and that revenue 'grows with trading activity' — the model is a commission on contracts traded through CDNA's Predictions product class, with Crypto.com FCM carrying the customer accounts, custody and settlement. Neither the 10-Q nor the call disclosed the revenue share ROLR keeps per dollar of contract volume, which leaves the sell-side modelling a business with no observable take-rate, no volume and no customer count.

The cost of getting here is visible across the P&L and cash-flow statement. Group advertising and promotions nearly doubled sequentially to $1,009k (42% of group revenue, from 18.5% in Q2 and 11.3% a year ago), of which $541k — 54% — was paid to the affiliated marketing partner Spike Up Media, with a further $333k related-party prepaid sitting on the balance sheet. Expensed product and software development was $247k (+17% YoY), and capitalised platform spend was roughly $1.7m in Q3 alone against ~$0.2m a year earlier, taking nine-month software and licence investment to $3,578k and net intangibles to $13.9m from $10.5m at December. G&A of $3,050k (+8% YoY) carries the new senior hires. Management said that the iOS launch 'unlocked our ability to go a little bit more full force with our marketing' and that 'for the moment, we're looking to get out there and spend' — Q4 marketing will be higher, not lower.

On distribution they have Lines.com, Forever Network and Leverage Game Media for audience reach and Spike Up for performance marketing, plus unnamed partners; the CEO says every channel is judged on conversion, customer quality, retention and revenue-to-cost, and claims a positive return on ad spend since 2021 across prior markets. We would note that the casino's own first-time-depositor count has fallen ~95% YoY, so that track record is historical rather than current, and that the related-party weighting of the spend makes third-party verification of CAC impossible from the outside. The CEO explicitly declined to say whether early CAC is within plan, declined to characterise promotional intensity beyond 'it's a very competitive space', and declined to commit to any interim KPI release before the FY26 results in March 2027.

Structurally, the company is moving to reduce its dependence on Crypto.com. ROLR US LLC's guaranteed-introducing-broker registration (NFA, 24 June) is exclusive to CDNA contracts for 24 months from the April 2026 collaboration agreement, i.e. to April 2028. On 11 November it formed ROLR FCM LLC and engaged Connamara Technologies to explore a futures-commission-merchant application; management's position is that FCM operations would fall outside the exclusivity, allowing the company to run an FCM alongside the introducing-broker relationship and to add other DCMs — hence the 12 November ProphetX agreement, which only becomes effective six months after FCM registration that has not yet been applied for. It has also registered with the NFA as a commodity trading advisor ahead of a new product release promised before the end of November, and floated DCM/DCO licences as longer-dated options. All of this is sensible optionality, but each step adds regulatory capital, compliance headcount and timeline risk for a company with ~$13m of cash.

On the market backdrop, management leans on Bernstein's ~$410bn 2026 volume estimate and $10tn-by-2035 projection, and presents competition (Meta's reported entry on the day of the call) as validation of the category's size. We would frame it differently: Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood, Crypto.com itself, DraftKings and FanDuel/CME are all competing for the same US sports-and-finance trader with marketing budgets that dwarf ROLR's quarterly revenue, and state-level litigation over sports event contracts is live enough that the CEO describes a state-targeted, 'hope for the best, plan for the worst' marketing plan. There is no segment guidance beyond 'major growth driver in 2027'. Our working assumption for Q4 is $0.1–0.4m of net revenue (estimate; ten weeks of trading, iOS-only mobile for half the period) against A&P of $1.3–1.8m, with the first meaningful read on funded accounts and volume per account not arriving until March.

report.sharePriceReaction: Results were released after the close on 13 Nov; ROLR had already fallen 7.1% to $3.03 in that session and slipped a further 7.3% to $2.81 after hours. On 16 Nov, the first full session post-results, the shares closed -15.5% (-$0.47) at $2.56 (intraday low ~$2.52, -16.8%), valuing the company at ~$28m — 81% below the January $13.21 registered-direct price and near the bottom of a $1.16–$33.68 52-week range.
